task: Cycle 2: acquired recurrent predictive features for persistent-readout finite-state processes

status_key.derived_proved: Elementary proof is provided in CYCLE2_REPORT.md; not externally reviewed.
status_key.interface_comparison: Derived comparison under a stated oracle; not a passive-data result.

claims.claim: For hidden Z=s·A and R independent Bernoulli(eta) readouts of the same Z in each reset episode, with theta=1-2eta>=beta>0 known, N=d+ceil(log2(2/delta)) random input episodes and odd R>=2 beta^-2 log(2N/delta) recover the exact dense mask s with probability >=1-delta by within-episode majority and GF(2) elimination.

costs.memory: O(d^2+R) working bits with streaming row reduction, plus model storage.
costs.model: d mask bits plus known rational eta.

claims.proof: Per-episode wrong-majority probability <=exp(-R beta^2/2); union bound <=delta/2. Uniform random input matrix rank failure <2^(d-N)<=delta/2.

claims.claim: Once s is recovered, the acquired feature phi_t(h)=e_{partial parity} in R^2 updates by a learned swap on each input bit and identity on each readout bit. For every fixed cut t and every bounded future task g, conditional expectation is phi_t(h)^T w_{t,g}, with ||phi_t||2=1 and ||w_{t,g}||2<=sqrt(2). The state retains one parity bit and public position, not the observed prefix.
claims.scope: Exact readout coefficients exist for all bounded g. For an efficiently evaluable g, each requested coefficient can be estimated by charged model simulation: M>=ceil((2 rho^2)^-1 log(8/delta)) futures per parity state, costing O(MH) simulator steps plus 2M evaluations of g per cut/task pair; with rational eta=a/b, bounded-rejection sampling costs O(MH L_eta log(MH/delta)) random-bit operations at stated high probability. This is not a uniform finite estimate for an uncountable task family.
claims.proof: The finite-state Markov property shows that at phase t the future conditional law depends on the history only through current parity and t. Each coefficient is in [0,1], giving the norm bound.

claims.claim: The equal-interface direct majority/GF(2) baseline receives exactly the same raw passive episodes and known parameters, executes exactly the same recovery computation, and outputs the same explicit model and recurrence at identical costs. No acquisition advantage over this control is claimed.
claims.costs: N(d+R) symbols; O(NR+Nd^2) bit operations; O(d^2+R) working bits.

claims.claim: A stronger conditional-sampling oracle can query each prefix A=e_i and receive R repeated readouts of s_i. Majority then recovers all mask bits without random-design linear algebra.
claims.costs: d chosen-prefix queries, dR returned readout symbols, d^2 prefix-specification bits, O(dR) majority work; R>=2 beta^-2 log(2d/delta) suffices up to constants.
claims.scope: This is not passive access; each chosen prefix has natural probability 2^-d.

claims.claim: Independent repeated measurements of the same latent parity are load-bearing. The theorem does not establish arbitrary finite-state/HMM acquisition, arbitrary low-rank conditional-sampling results, or the teacher-assisted A06 recurrence target. Historical novelty is not cleared.

sources.title: Astra N13 persistent-readout route and local predictive margins
sources.use: Context for the repeated-readout class. CYCLE2_REPORT.md independently derives the mask recovery, recurrence and task-readout costs; this internal source is not treated as external validation.
